title: Strict HA number-theory campaign: arithmetic substrate through finite CRT

source_specification.role: Byte-identical in-repository capture of the controlling design document at campaign start; this manifest records the executable K0-K6 and M1-M5 tranche.

authority.object_language: 0, S, +, *, = with intuitionistic connectives and quantifiers
authority.candidate_policy: Candidate factories are isolated, dependency-curried proof bodies. They are not public theorems until an empty-context certificate is checked and deliberately admitted.
authority.definition_policy: Every surface definition must expand to the unchanged object language before kernel checking.

status_vocabulary.existing_public_core: A substantial reusable core is already admitted in the public object-level HA registry; the recorded remaining gap is not thereby claimed complete.
status_vocabulary.candidate_seed: An isolated, non-public proof candidate directly seeds the next layer; its exact theorem-level evidence is recorded separately and never implies public admission.
status_vocabulary.new: No representation-compatible implementation of the package target has been selected yet.
status_vocabulary.blocked_on_dependency: Work is deliberately held behind an earlier incomplete package named in depends_on_layers.

status_vocabulary.public_checked: A complete empty-context certificate checks intuitionistically and the theorem is deliberately enrolled in the public registry.
status_vocabulary.closed_checked_candidate: A complete empty-context certificate checks intuitionistically, but the theorem is intentionally absent from the public registry.
status_vocabulary.body_checked_candidate: Only the dependency-curried candidate body has been checked.
status_vocabulary.planned: The statement and dependency location are frozen, but no checked proof body exists.
status_vocabulary.blocked_on_dependency: A named earlier theorem or representation gate prevents honest proof work.
status_vocabulary.legacy_late_encoding: Checked material may be reused later but cannot be the campaign's foundational representation.

validation_gates.scope: Check strict JSON shape, stable identifiers, dependency order, source paths, public references, candidate references, and the K3 anti-circularity invariant.
Parse each expanded target as a closed formula over the unchanged Peano object language and compare its readable definition expansion.
validation_gates.quick_command: Run the layer's focused statement and definition tests.

validation_gates.scope: Replay the dependency-curried body constructively, reject DNE, record proof size and depth, and reject a nearby false mutation.
validation_gates.quick_command: Run only the candidate module's focused pytest file.

validation_gates.scope: Verify declared dependencies exist, precede the theorem, are sufficient for body replay, and do not introduce forbidden representation cycles; for closed candidates, build and record the exact empty-context closure without registry mutation.
validation_gates.quick_command: Run candidate topology, dependency-order, and empty-context closure receipt tests.

validation_gates.scope: After a deterministic empty-context closure receipt exists, deliberately enroll the theorem in the public registry and replay it through the post-enrollment public path.
validation_gates.quick_command: Review the registry admission change, then run focused public replay and mutation tests.

validation_gates.scope: Regenerate source-derived catalog, vault, book, explorer, and snapshot artifacts, then run their check modes.
validation_gates.quick_command: Run the existing arithmetic knowledge-base and generated-artifact check commands.

validation_gates.scope: Run large closure, resource, mutation, and browser-memory checks on WMI only after all local gates pass.
validation_gates.quick_command: Submit a receipt-pinned WMI validation job.

representation_invariants.k3_foundational_encoding: HA-K3-SIGNED-1 selects parity-interleaved canonical signed naturals and HA-K3-PAIR-1 selects doubled-Cantor pairs plus successor-tagged cells independently of CRT and Godel-beta coding; the uniform computation-trace, list, and finite-map representations remain to be selected
representation_invariants.legacy_beta_role: Existing beta-coded sequence, fold, factorization, and QR theorems remain valid public HA results and reusable arithmetic evidence, but they do not discharge K3 and may not be dependencies of K3's first pair/list representation.
canonical_acceptance: decoding is functional on valid codes
equality of represented objects is decidable
operations preserve validity and meet their expanded specifications
host elaboration data compile to object-language codes

layers.title: Object language and proof calculus
layers.target: Fix first-order intuitionistic logic with equality over 0, S, +, * and formula-specific induction, with explicit certificates checked by the HA kernel.
layers.remaining_gap: Freeze a campaign-specific exported-certificate manifest and keep classical checking outside every native release gate.

layers.title: Decidable bounded arithmetic
layers.target: Provide decidability and reflection for equality, order, bounded divisibility, primality, finite membership, and general bounded formulas.
layers.remaining_gap: The reusable decision theorems are public, but no general object-level Delta-zero reflection compiler has yet been frozen for the campaign.

layers.title: Primitive-recursive definitional extensions
layers.target: Supply graph formulas, functionality, and conservative readable interfaces for exponentiation, factorial, quotient, remainder, coding, evaluation, and finite folds.
layers.remaining_gap: Individual graph relations are public; a reviewed generic conservative-symbol and elimination discipline still needs to be packaged and tested.

layers.title: Finite-data coding
layers.target: Build canonical primitive-recursive codes for pairs, signed integers, explicit-length lists, sorted sets, matrices, permutations, finite functions, and proof-relevant bijections without using CRT or a Godel-beta construction.

candidate_modules.role: Closed-checked but non-public K1-only parity separation and even-half uniqueness prerequisites for the parity-interleaved signed decoder.
Closed-checked but non-public constructors, totality, normality, functionality, zero characterization, and universal validity for RFC HA-K3-SIGNED-1.
Closed-checked but non-public extensionality bridge between literal parity-interleaved code equality and cross-sum equality of decoded signed values.
Closed-checked but non-public constructive normalization of arbitrary balanced natural pairs plus decoder transport and the cross-sum helper.
Closed-checked but non-public extensionality, functionality, and exact zero characterization for canonical SignedBalance normalization.
Closed-checked but non-public decoder bridges, totality, functionality, zero, symmetry, and involution for the canonical SignedNegate graph.
Closed-checked but non-public decoder-equation bridges, totality, and literal-output functionality for the canonical SignedAdd graph.
Closed-checked but non-public commutativity, two-sided zero identity, and two-sided additive-inverse graph laws for canonical SignedAdd.
Closed-checked but non-public cross-sum composition, decoded-equation reassociation, and exact graph associativity for canonical SignedAdd.
Closed-checked but non-public decoder-equation bridges, totality, and literal-output functionality for the canonical SignedMul graph.
Closed-checked but non-public commutativity, two-sided zero annihilation, and two-sided signed-one identity laws for canonical SignedMul.
Closed-checked but non-public pair-product transport, component reassociation, decoded-equation reassociation, and exact graph associativity for canonical SignedMul.
Closed-checked but non-public additive shuffling, balanced-output composition, decoded component distribution, and exact left and right graph distributivity for canonical SignedMul.
Closed-checked but non-public decoder-equation bridges, totality, and literal-output functionality for the canonical SignedNatScale graph.
Closed-checked but non-public scalar cross-sum transport, decoded-equation composition, zero and one scaling, and exact graph composition for canonical SignedNatScale.
Closed-checked but non-public balanced-equation transport, both directions between four-natural BalancedBezout witnesses and canonical SignedBezout codes, and their packaged equivalence.

layers.remaining_gap: The parity-interleaved decoder, decoded-code extensionality, total functional SignedBalance normalization, total functional involutive SignedNegate graph, the complete SignedAdd and SignedMul graph laws, D07 SignedNatScale, and both D08 BalancedBezout/SignedBezout conversion directions now have deterministic empty-context candidate receipts without division, remainder, beta, or CRT dependencies. HA-K3-PAIR-1 freezes a non-circular pair/cell design but has no proof candidates yet. Deliberate public admission, an optional signed-code equality alias, pair/cell proofs, an independent uniform computation-trace/list/map encoding, and list recursion remain; gcd packaging stays a separate K4 client because its public dependency closure reaches division.

layers.title: Division and Euclidean algorithms
layers.target: Provide canonical quotient and remainder, gcd, lcm, extended Euclid, balanced Bezout coefficients, and executable specifications.

candidate_modules.role: Closed-checked but non-public existence, functionality, and unique-existence package for the canonical relational gcd predicate, derived without zero side conditions from the public IsGCD interface.
Closed-checked but non-public K4 client combining public relational-gcd and balanced-Bezout existence with the strict-K3 canonical SignedBezout bridge.
Closed-checked but non-public equality characterizations for canonical gcd at zero and one, plus function-style symmetry for independently selected relational witnesses.
Closed-checked but non-public convenience consequences of the admitted universal-property IsLCM core, including divisibility specializations and zero/one packages.

layers.remaining_gap: The reviewed universal-property lcm core, lcm totality and unique existence, and the gcd-times-lcm product identity are public. Canonical gcd packaging and boundary laws, canonical signed Bezout coefficients, ten LCM convenience consequences, and an executable Euclidean graph remain outside the public interface.

layers.title: Prime factorization and valuations
layers.target: Provide least-prime-divisor search, Euclid's lemma, sorted prime-factor lists, uniqueness, and p-adic valuation algebra.
layers.remaining_gap: Prime-divisor, Euclid, and beta-coded FTA theorems are public. The factorization interface must migrate to K3 canonical lists, and valuation existence, uniqueness, and algebra are absent.

layers.title: Finite sums, products, and cardinality
layers.target: Develop representation-independent finite folds, reindexing, partitions, duplicate-free lists, permutations, pigeonhole, double counting, and product cancellation on K3 data.
layers.remaining_gap: The checked beta-coded combinatorics remains reusable as arithmetic guidance, but the campaign package is blocked until K3 supplies its non-circular canonical list API.

layers.title: Modular inverse criterion
layers.target: For positive m, prove that a is coprime to m exactly when there is a unique u below m with a*u congruent to 1 modulo m, and expose a conservative invmod graph.
layers.remaining_gap: The exact bounded-existence, converse, uniqueness, and iff criterion are public. A conservative invmod graph and its interface to HA-K3-SIGNED-1 remain for the full executable package.

layers.title: Classification of linear congruences
layers.target: Classify solvability of a*x congruent to b modulo positive m by gcd divisibility and construct the duplicate-free list of exactly gcd(a,m) canonical solutions.
layers.remaining_gap: The arithmetic reduction is available, but the constructive solver, obstruction witness, K3 solution list, distinctness proof, and exact cardinality wait on M1 and K6.

layers.title: Binary Chinese remainder theorem
layers.target: For coprime positive m and n, construct the unique x below m*n satisfying two arbitrary congruences, with an expanded first-order specification.
layers.remaining_gap: The public binary CRT supplies balanced-congruence existence. Canonical normalization below m*n, simultaneous uniqueness, executable output, and the M1-based statement remain.

layers.title: Finite Chinese remainder theorem
layers.target: Fold binary CRT over a K3 list of pairwise-coprime positive moduli and residues, producing the unique representative below their product.
layers.remaining_gap: Legacy beta-prefix CRT lemmas are public but cannot found K3. The K3 list fold, invariant, empty/singleton cases, uniqueness, rejection, and permutation-invariant specification wait on K3, K6, and M3.

layers.title: Generalized Chinese remainder theorem
layers.target: Decide a finite noncoprime congruence system by pairwise gcd compatibility, returning either a canonical solution modulo the lcm or an explicit incompatible pair.

candidate_modules.role: Closed-checked but non-public generalized-CRT congruence foundation: additive cancellation, zero modulus, scaling and nonzero unscaling, pairwise solution congruence, necessary gcd compatibility, and its constructive incompatibility obstruction.

Closed-checked but non-public M5a binary sufficiency ladder: nonzero coprime gcd cofactors, a shared bounded remainder, coprime-CRT scaling and lifting, compatible-system construction, and the nonzero-modulus solvability criterion.

layers.remaining_gap: The K4 relational LCM core is public, and 15 generalized-CRT foundation and M5a binary rows now have deterministic empty-context receipts. For nonzero moduli, gcd compatibility is proved necessary and sufficient for a common solution. Zero-modulus wrappers, uniqueness modulo relational lcm, canonical bounded representatives, executable incompatibility decisions, and the K3 finite-system fold remain.
